newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.58 pct March 16-April 14.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.58 pct March 16-April 14.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) rose to 0.58 percent between March 16 and April 14 compared with 0.34 percent in the prior four-week period, a Fipe official said.
Fipe chief Juarez Rizzieri said the rise in the index, which measures inflation in the Sao Paulo area, was due mostly to climbing clothing prices linked to the arrival of autumn in Brazil.
He projected further rises in clothing prices would bring April's inflation to one percent.
In the four-week period food, housing and health care prices also posted strong gains while transport and personal expenses dipped.
Rizzieri released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for March 16 through April 14:
- Food: 1.01 pct rise in the month
- Housing: 0.56 pct rise in the month
- Transportation: -0.26 pct drop in the month
- Personal expenses: -0.18 pct drop in the month
- Clothing: 1.58 pct rise in the month
- Health care: 0.83 pct rise in the month
- Education: 0.16 pct rise in the month
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
